answer: Reciprocal Delivery Lattice. Each identity must originate traffic whose inter-arrival gaps fall on a shared umber schedule, and every message cites the prior gap it answers. Nodes only forward traffic whose timing matches the lattice phase they observe. To fake many identities, an attacker must run each one long enough to accumulate a verifiable timing history and cross the reef of mixed-phase relays, paying continuous bandwidth and latency costs per fake identity. At scale this becomes a summit of parallel real-time channels that cannot be cheaply faked.
